turns.text: *squeeze through a gap where a storm drain grate's rusted through, shoulder scraping cold concrete on both sides. air changes the second the body clears it — outside smell washes away, replaced by oil, exhaust-ash, and a flat mineral cold that never sees sun. paws land on smooth concrete, ears flattening against a low mechanical thrum that never stops, felt through the pads before it's heard.*

level B3 breathes the same stale hum it always does, sodium light flickering along a ceiling strip half its bulbs dead, three floors of parked steel stacked overhead like sleeping animals

far wall: a ramp curling up and out of sight, wet tire-tracks drying in long fading stripes, a NekoCorp maintenance drone's searchlight sweeping the upper ramp on its slow patrol loop — thirty-second interval, same as every night, same as every level

rat-smell threads low along the drainage channel cut into the floor, old, thin, mixed with battery-acid and standing water

nothing moving yet at this level. the hum underneath everything is the building itself, arcology towers breathing through their foundations, patient and endless

*low walk between two rows of parked delivery pods, weight kept off the drainage channel, nose reading each vehicle in turn — cold rubber, dead battery, cold rubber, dead battery. one breaks the pattern three pods down: heat radiating off its underside, a smell sharper than the rest, sweet and chemical.*

third pod's coolant line has split somewhere low, dripping slow onto the concrete in a widening dark stain, sweet antifreeze-smell cutting clean through the garage's usual flat cold

pod's own systems don't register it — running a diagnostic loop, status light blinking amber under the chassis, waiting on a maintenance ticket nobody's filed yet

the puddle's warm, actually warm, heat still bleeding out of the engine block into the concrete around it, a rare patch of comfort in a building that doesn't otherwise care if you're cold

>> pod status: FAULT — awaiting service
>> ETA: unscheduled

/\_/\        [ ENERGY: LOW ]
  ( >.< )       [ ]  [ ]  [ ]  [ ]
   > ~ <        one bar left, keep moving

*settle into the warm ring around the puddle without touching the antifreeze itself, belly pressed to sun-less concrete gone almost pleasant. eyes half-close for one long breath before a second smell cuts through the sweetness — copper, old, gone brown at the edges. blood, not fresh, coming from behind the next row.*

behind the next row, wedged between a support pillar and a parked pod's rear wheel, something small and gray lies still — a rat, throat opened clean, the kind of kill that doesn't struggle twice

no claw marks in the concrete around it, no drag trail, no scent of any cat's paws in the blood — this wasn't hunted, it was caught, and the thing that caught it left almost nothing of itself behind except one hairline scratch across the pillar's base, metal-bright, too straight to be a claw

     ⚠ PEST CONTROL — active unit, autonomous, quiet

somewhere on this level, a small drone is doing exactly the job it was built for, and it hasn't finished its patrol yet

*backs off the kill in three quiet steps, tail dropping low instead of lashing, every instinct saying smaller and quieter than before. angles away from the pillar toward a bank of elevator doors at the garage's far end, moving along the wall where shadow pools deepest. six feet from the doors, a smell stops the paws cold — bitter herb, rubbed low across the threshold, unmistakable.*

elevator bank sits recessed into the wall, three sets of doors gone dull with grime, call button glowing a tired orange that's flickered that color for months

the threshold mark is fresh, laid down within the day, bitter-herb cut with something sharper this time — ammonia-sting, deliberate, a scent built to carry through diesel and rat and antifreeze alike

     ⚠ CROSSING: active claim, elevator bank, all three doors

underneath the doors, felt through the floor more than heard, one elevator car groans somewhere in the shaft above, cables singing faint under tension — whoever marked this ground uses that shaft themselves, uses it often enough to own the smell of the whole bank

no fur in sight, no eyes watching from the shadows past the doors — just the claim, laid down loud, meant to be found before its owner ever needs to show up in person

/\___/\
    ( o   o )   >> scanning...
     )  Y  (    >> ears: antenna mod v2
    (   |   )
     \_____/

*doesn't cross the marked threshold, peels off toward a service hatch beside the elevator bank instead, gap wide enough to squeeze a shoulder through. inside: a maintenance shaft running straight up, thick cable bundles bolted along one wall, a service ladder rusted but climbable bolted to the other. cold air drops down from somewhere far above, carrying a thin thread of warmth and light riding underneath it.*

shaft runs twelve floors clean, dark except for a service-light strip blinking dim red every third landing, cables thrumming faint with current where paws would brush against them climbing

somewhere above, the elevator car passes on its own track, sealed off from the shaft you're in but close enough that its motor-whine rattles loose bolts in the ladder rail as it goes

near the top, past a dozen landings, the cold air thread breaks — warmer, carrying scorched-plastic and old coffee and the particular blue-white flicker of a screen left running all night

     >> rooftop-adjacent level: unlisted terminal, unsecured

the ladder holds, rung after rung, patient the way old rusted metal always is right up until it isn't — and the warm light at the top keeps still, waiting, indifferent to whether anything ever climbs high enough to reach it
